title: QUEST: An Open Deep-Research Agent
hook: A fully open Deep Research agent trained on ~32 H100s and ~8K synthetic samples — recipe, code, weights, and data all released, and reportedly competitive with frontier closed systems.
key_points: QUEST-35B, from Ohio State University's NLP group, is an open-source Deep Research agent.
Trained with roughly 32 H100 GPUs and about 8K synthetic samples — modest by frontier standards.
The team open-sourced the full stack: training recipe, code, model weights, and datasets.
Reported as competitive with several frontier Deep Research systems on benchmarks.
content_html: "Deep Research" — agents that plan multi-step web investigations and write up sourced answers — has mostly lived inside closed products. Ohio State University's NLP group released QUEST-35B to change that: an open-source Deep Research agent with the entire pipeline laid bare.
extra_html:
What was released

Per the announcement, QUEST-35B was trained using roughly 32 H100 GPUs and about 8,000 synthetic samples — a notably small footprint for this class of system — and the team open-sourced the training recipe, code, model weights, and datasets together. Reported benchmark results put it competitive with several frontier Deep Research systems.

Why it matters

Reproducibility is the point. When a capability ships only as a closed feature, the community can't study how it's actually built or where it breaks. A fully open recipe trained on modest compute lowers the barrier to entry and turns Deep Research into something researchers can dissect, fine-tune, and improve — while leaving open the real question of how far open agents still trail the best closed systems. (Details here come from the release post rather than a peer-reviewed paper.)

related.title: Harness-1: RL for Search Agents with State-Externalizing Harnesses
related.hook: Stop making the policy remember everything. Harness-1 moves a search agent's bookkeeping into the environment, so RL only has to learn the decisions that matter.

related.title: ReAct: Reasoning + Acting
related.hook: Thinking alone can drift; acting alone is blind. ReAct interleaves reasoning with tool calls so an LLM can plan, look things up, and correct course — the template for agents.

related.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning
related.hook: DeepSeek shows strong reasoning can emerge from RL on verifiable rewards with minimal supervised data - and those reasoning traces can be distilled into smaller models.
